To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the laser reprocessing of the cermet coatings can provide a significant increase in the corrosion resistance, by improving the coating hardness and reducing the coating consumption rate, induced by the high-temperature corrosive attack.
laser reprocessing can improve the type II hot corrosion behavior of cermet coatings by enhancing their surface hardness and reducing their material consumption rate.
laser-sealing of cermet coatings, can be an effective way of increasing their hot corrosion resistance, in the presence aggressive environments, such as the one used in this study.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the optimization of the laser reprocessing conditions, in terms of laser power and scanning velocity, to improve the hot corrosion resistance and the mechanical properties of the thermal-sprayed coatings.

the development of a new laser-sealing technology for thermal-sprayed coatings, with the aim of increasing their corrosion resistance, and with the investigation of the effect of the sealing treatment on the microstructure, hardness and corrosion behavior of different coatings, with the purpose of providing a better understanding of the mechanism of action of the laser treatment.
the development of laser-sealed thermal-sprayed cermet coatings with improved resistance to type II hot corrosion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the laser-sealed coatings exhibited a significant increase in the hot corrosion resistance of the as-sprayed coatings, which was mainly related to a reduction of the material consumption rate.
the laser-sealed cermet coatings can provide a substantial increase in service life in comparison to non-laser sealed ones.
laser-sealing is a viable and cost-effective technique to increase the hot corrosion resistance of thermally-sprayed coatings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the type II hot corrosion degradation mechanism is not modified by the laser sealing but, the overall corrosion rate is significantly decreased.

, the laser sealing process is a promising method to increase the corrosion resistance of thermal-sprayed coatings, but the effectiveness of the process strongly depends on the coating microstructure and composition.

, the high temperature corrosion behavior of the laser sealed cermet coatings is strongly dependent on the coating microstructure, the laser treatment parameters, and the composition of the aggressive species.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the hot corrosion resistance of thermal sprayed coatings could be significantly increased by laser reprocessing, provided that the latter is optimized to minimize the formation of a molten pool, which could induce the formation of cracks and pores.

laser reprocessing can be a valuable tool in optimizing the hot corrosion performance of cermet thermal-sprayed coatings, in particular when the coating is characterized by a relatively low hardness and/or a high porosity level.

, in order to improve the hot corrosion resistance of the coatings, a laser sealing treatment should be performed in order to increase the surface hardness of the coating and, consequently, to reduce the material consumption rate.
